justification: The opening fixes the familiar rule — "the mixed-flow has a fixed reputation: the tall machine with the ducts inside is the one that burns" and "The explanation is as settled as the count" — and the rest of the piece is three men disagreeing about the why: Calverend "thinks the count is right and the reason is wrong", Grendisham says "the clock is the weak joint in the argument", and Steadgrove would "move it one step further out, to the contract". A is unsupported (no price series is tracked across the nine harvests) and C is absent entirely. B names only Grendisham's single objection ("nobody was there to see it early"), a strand of the dispute rather than its subject.

The swab result is stated once and plainly: "His team swabbed the duct faces of twenty-six machines that had never burned; per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent." That contradicts A directly, and C is never addressed (no claim about newest ducts). D misreads the dispute: Grendisham disputes the swabs on seasonality — "her crews still pull buckets of fines in February from machines that swabbed clean in September" — not on sample size, and the writer treats them as the strong evidence ("The swabs are hard to walk past").

Grendisham's objection is that the log's second timestamp is a discovery time, not an ignition time: "The other time in the file is the moment the call came in. On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught." A is the opposite of her point — she says pairing the two numbers is why "of course the fire looks late". B and D are not addressed: she never restricts the log to her own service customers and never says the times were not meant as evidence.

Steadgrove's date sort is the implication: "Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine, he argues, and the machine stops mattering. Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest, when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator's delivery window is closing" — a pressure of the calendar, not of the equipment. B overstates the count (49 of 61 leaves twelve fires outside the stretch, which is not "hardly a fire"); C is contradicted by "Steadgrove's is not the mutual's to give, since the deduction schedule belongs to the elevators"; D is never claimed — "trucks waiting" appears only in the closing question about one operator, and no arrival-versus-capacity comparison is made.

The writer's verdict is explicit: "Grendisham's objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these" and "Calverend's account fits the evidence without having been tested by it." That kills A (the objections stand) and B (she does adjudicate — "The swabs are hard to walk past"). D is contradicted by the reservation about his remedy: "Whether writing a run-on clause into next year's policies would be worth anything turns on something nobody has worked out how to check."

Sekvensen står i första stycket: "Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten, när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan. Malmen grävdes upp i smala rutor, lades i högar på fastare mark och fick ligga ute vintern över ... Först därefter rostades den på en bädd av ved." A vänder både årstiden och ordningen (rostning före hög). B motsägs av "Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt", och D av "Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte."

Tolvsäter's first clear result states both the effect and its mechanism: "De blåsningar som drevs hårdast, med tätare bälgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet, och klumpen sprack under släggan i stället för att låta sig sträckas." B inverts the direction of the relationship. C overstates it — the harder runs gave brittler blooms, not failure of "samtliga blåsningar". D belongs to the excavation description ("Innan den kunde fyllas måste den torkas långsamt"), not to the trials, whose reported findings are the two above.

The solid-state reduction is named as the governing fact and is then explicitly made to govern both consequences: "Det är hantverkets utgångspunkt. Järnet reducerades i fast form ... Ur detta följer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom. En blåsning gav några kilo järn" and "Tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efteråt, i räckningen." A is contradicted by the dating "tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet"; B inverts the technologies, since it is the later hyttan that "krävde vattenkraft"; C is contradicted by "uppteckningarna, som är utförliga om vem som ägde vad, säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen."

The trials reinterpret the iron-rich slag as a precondition rather than a loss: "Och den järnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lägre järnhalt blir trögflytande vid de temperaturer en sådan ugn orkar hålla ... Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet." A is Krokvall's reading of "dålig kontroll", which is precisely what "det är tolkningen av dem som försöken talar emot" rejects. C is contradicted by "Krokvalls mätvärden har ingen ifrågasatt", and D by "varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen" — the text leaves the yield variation unexplained.
